ActivityOut.description:
One entry on a lead/customer/deal timeline. `actor_name` and
`actor_email` are denormalized off the User JOIN so the UI
doesn't N+1; `type` is the short slug — frontend maps to a
translated label + icon.
ActivityOut.title: ActivityOut

AiCreditStatus.description:
Current-month AI-credit usage for the caller's org (1 credit = 1 AI
action). `limit`/`remaining` are null on unlimited plans.
AiCreditStatus.title: AiCreditStatus

ApiKeyCreate.description:
Admin mints a Public-API key for the current org.

`scopes` is coarse for v1: `read` (GET) and/or `write` (mutations).
Defaults to read-only — the least-privilege default, so a key that's
only meant to pull data can't accidentally be granted write. An empty
list is rejected (a scopeless key could do nothing). `expires_at` is
optional; omit for a non-expiring key.
ApiKeyCreate.title: ApiKeyCreate

ApiKeyCreated.description:
One-time response on POST /api/api-keys carrying the plaintext
`token`. Copy it now — it is hashed at rest and can't be shown again.
ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated

ApiKeyOut.description:
Public view of an API key — the secret token is NEVER here. The
plaintext is shown ONCE on create (ApiKeyCreated) and is otherwise
unrecoverable. `display_prefix` is the non-secret label for the list.
ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut

ApiKeyScope.description:
Coarse-grained permission a Public-API key carries.

`read`  — GET only (idempotent, safe verbs).
`write` — everything `read` can do, plus create/update/delete.
A key stores a SET of scopes (`["read"]` or `["read","write"]`);
the bearer dependency maps the request's HTTP method to the scope
it requires. Intentionally coarse for v1 — per-resource scopes
(`leads:read`) can be added later without a schema change since
scopes live in a JSON column, not a Postgres enum.
ApiKeyScope.title: ApiKeyScope

ApplyTemplateIn.description: Optional knobs; the wizard usually sends an empty body.
ApplyTemplateIn.title: ApplyTemplateIn

AuditLogOut.description:
One row of the audit ledger, surfaced via the admin audit UI.
`actor_email` and `actor_name` are denormalized from the User
JOIN so the page renders without N+1 lookups.
AuditLogOut.title: AuditLogOut

AutomationAction.description:
What an automation rule does when it fires.

All three are fully internal (no external/paid dependency): spawn a
follow-up Task, drop an in-app Notification on the owner's bell, or
auto-advance a deal's stage. Email dispatch is a deliberate later
slice — it needs the templated-email surface and recipient
resolution, so it's kept out of v1 rather than half-built.
AutomationAction.title: AutomationAction

AutomationTrigger.description:
What fires an automation rule.

The event-family members map 1:1 to `app.events.EventType` slugs —
the wildcard outbox subscriber (`app.automations.run_event_automations`)
matches a fired event's type to rules carrying the same trigger. The
`lead_stale` member is the lone TIME-based trigger: it has no outbox
event, it's evaluated by the `scan_stale_leads` cron instead.
AutomationTrigger.title: AutomationTrigger

CheckoutRequest.description:
UpgradeRequest + currency (plan.md §6). Local subclass so the
shared schemas module stays untouched; defaults to EUR so existing
frontend calls keep working unchanged.
CheckoutRequest.title: CheckoutRequest

CompanyRollup.description:
What the Account detail page renders: the company plus the
contacts (customers + leads) and deals that hang off it.
CompanyRollup.title: CompanyRollup

ContractCreate.description:
A new draft contract. Unlike a quote there are no line items — a
contract carries a single agreed `value`; itemisation (if any) lives
on the linked source quote. `quote_id` is optional so a contract can
be drafted free-standing, but when present the route can later copy
over title/value defaults.
ContractCreate.title: ContractCreate

ContractStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a contract / agreement (ADR-016).

State machine (enforced in `app/api/contracts.py`):
    draft ──send──▶ sent ──sign──▶ signed ──activate──▶ active
                                      │                    │
                                      └───terminate────────┴──▶ terminated
    active ──(time)──▶ expired   (set by a future cron, no endpoint)

`draft` is the only editable state. Once sent the agreement is
immutable — a "re-issue with changes" clones it into a new version
(the old row keeps its terminal state and points at the new one via
`superseded_by`), exactly like Quote. `terminate` is the early-exit
path from a signed or active contract; `expired` is the natural
end-of-term state (reached by a scheduled sweep, mirroring how a
quote expires — there is no manual transition for it).
ContractStatus.title: ContractStatus

ContractUpdate.description:
Draft-only edits. The route rejects edits to a non-draft contract
(a sent/signed revision is immutable — resend creates a new version
instead). All fields optional.
ContractUpdate.title: ContractUpdate

ConversationAssign.description:
Assign a thread to an agent — or release it back to the shared queue.

``assignee_id`` is the target agent (must belong to the caller's org); send
``null`` to unassign. The field is required so the intent is always explicit
(unlike ``ConversationLink``, there is no "leave untouched" case here).
ConversationAssign.title: ConversationAssign

ConversationChannel.description:
Messaging channel a conversation rides. Only `whatsapp` is wired in
phase 1; `instagram` / `messenger` are declared ahead of their adapters
(same Meta Graph + webhook layer) so the schema doesn't churn later.
ConversationChannel.title: ConversationChannel

ConversationConvert.description:
Spin up a CRM record from a WhatsApp thread, then link the thread to it.

``target`` picks Lead vs Customer. The new record's name defaults from the
contact's WhatsApp profile name (first token → ``first_name``, the rest →
``last_name``); pass ``first_name``/``last_name`` to override. The contact's
``wa_id`` always seeds the phone in E.164 (``+<digits>``).
ConversationConvert.title: ConversationConvert

ConversationLink.description:
Attach (or detach) a conversation from a CRM record.

Omit a field to leave it untouched; send it as ``null`` to clear the link.
The route reads ``model_fields_set`` to distinguish the two cases.
ConversationLink.title: ConversationLink

service_window_expires_at.description:
When the 24h free-form window closes (None if never opened). The UI
uses this to warn the agent before a free-form send gets rejected.
service_window_expires_at.title: Service Window Expires At

service_window_open.description: Whether free-form (non-template) sends are currently allowed.
service_window_open.title: Service Window Open

ConversationStatusUpdate.description:
Move a thread through its lifecycle: ``open`` ⇄ ``closed`` ⇄ ``archived``.
A ``closed`` thread auto-reopens on the next inbound message; ``archived``
stays put until reopened by hand.
ConversationStatusUpdate.title: ConversationStatusUpdate

CustomFieldType.description:
The shapes a per-org custom field can take. The value drives both
server-side coercion/validation (`app/custom_fields.py`) and the
widget the frontend renders. `select`/`multiselect` consult the
definition's `options` list; everything else ignores it.
CustomFieldType.title: CustomFieldType

DocumentTemplateCreate.description:
A new reusable template body with `{{ token }}` merge fields. The
body is operator-authored text — tokens are substituted (allow-list),
never evaluated. `doc_type` defaults to `contract` (the only target
wired today).
DocumentTemplateCreate.title: DocumentTemplateCreate

DocumentTemplateUpdate.description: Partial edit of a template. All fields optional.
DocumentTemplateUpdate.title: DocumentTemplateUpdate

DocumentType.description:
The kind of document a merge-field template targets (ADR-016).

Only `contract` is wired today (templates seed `Contract.body`);
the enum exists so quote / invoice templates can be added later
without a schema change to the discriminator.
DocumentType.title: DocumentType

DuplicateGroup.description: A set of 2+ records that collide on one signal.
DuplicateGroup.title: DuplicateGroup

DuplicateRecord.description:
One candidate row in a duplicate group — a compact summary for the
merge picker (never the full entity).
DuplicateRecord.title: DuplicateRecord

EmailVerifyConfirm.description:
Body of POST /api/auth/verify-email/confirm. The `token` is the
URL-safe credential from the verification email; confirming it marks
the bound user's email verified and starts a session.
EmailVerifyConfirm.title: EmailVerifyConfirm

EmailVerifyResend.description:
Body of POST /api/auth/verify-email/resend. Always responds 204 (no
enumeration); a fresh link is only minted when the email maps to an
active, not-yet-verified user.
EmailVerifyResend.title: EmailVerifyResend

EntityTagsOut.description: The tags attached to one entity — used to render chips on list rows.
EntityTagsOut.title: EntityTagsOut

FileAttachmentDownloadOut.description:
Short-lived presigned download URL the SPA hands to the
browser (typically via `window.location = url`).
FileAttachmentDownloadOut.title: FileAttachmentDownloadOut

FileAttachmentOut.description:
Metadata row for one attachment. Blob lives in S3 — the
download URL is fetched on demand via `/api/attachments/{id}/download`
so listing doesn't leak presigned URLs into the SPA's HTML.
FileAttachmentOut.title: FileAttachmentOut

FxRatesOut.description:
Current EUR-based FX rates for the display-currency layer (roadmap #1).

`rates` is "1 EUR = rate[ccy]" (e.g. USD ≈ 1.08), always including EUR:1.
`as_of` is the ECB publication date (null for the static fallback).
FxRatesOut.title: FxRatesOut

ImportEntityType.description:
Which CRM entity a bulk import targets (ADR-016 imports slice).

Only the two contact-shaped entities are importable today — they
carry the email/phone keys the dedupe logic matches on. Deals/tasks
would need a customer-linkage resolution step, deferred.
ImportEntityType.title: ImportEntityType

ImportJobOut.description:
One bulk-import job — created `pending`, polled by the SPA until
`status` is terminal (`completed` / `failed`). The counters and
`error_report` are zero/empty until the worker finishes.
ImportJobOut.title: ImportJobOut

ImportMode.description:
How a row that matches an existing record is handled.

`create`  — matched rows are skipped (insert-only; safest default).
`upsert`  — matched rows have their non-empty columns updated.
Match key is `(org, lower(email))` first, then normalised phone.
ImportMode.title: ImportMode

ImportStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an import job (driven by the `process_import` worker).

    pending ──▶ processing ──▶ completed
                            └▶ failed   (fatal parse/read error)

A `completed` job may still carry per-row errors in `error_report` —
`failed` is reserved for a whole-file failure (unreadable, unknown
columns, empty), where nothing was imported.
ImportStatus.title: ImportStatus

ImportTemplateOut.description:
Canonical column headers for an entity's import template (a `*`
suffix marks required columns), so the SPA can offer a starter file.
ImportTemplateOut.title: ImportTemplateOut

InteractiveButton.description:
One reply button. `id` comes back verbatim in the inbound button_reply,
so it's the stable handle automations key off; `title` is the visible label
(Meta caps it at 20 chars).
InteractiveButton.title: InteractiveButton

InteractiveRow.description: One selectable row in a list section.
InteractiveRow.title: InteractiveRow

InteractiveSection.description: A titled group of list rows.
InteractiveSection.title: InteractiveSection

InviteAcceptRequest.description:
Body for POST /api/auth/register-with-invite — same shape as the
plain register payload except `email` is fixed by the invite.
InviteAcceptRequest.title: InviteAcceptRequest

InviteCreate.description: Admin → invite a new member by email + the role they get on join.
InviteCreate.title: InviteCreate

InviteOut.description:
What the admin sees back when listing or creating invites.

`invite_url` is populated only on the CREATE response — listing
endpoints don't re-expose it because the admin already has the link
from the create response (and re-sending it would be a job for a
"resend invite" endpoint, not a list).
InviteOut.title: InviteOut

InvitePreview.description:
Public view of an invite — what /api/invites/{token} returns to a
not-yet-registered visitor. Carries just enough context (org name,
email it was sent to, role they'll get) so the registration page
can render a "You're joining Acme Corp as Sales Agent" header.
InvitePreview.title: InvitePreview

LeadConvertIn.description: Optional overrides — sensible defaults come from the lead.
LeadConvertIn.title: LeadConvertIn

LlmUsageSummary.description:
Per-org LLM token usage over a recent window, for cost observability.
Scoped to the caller's org by RLS; admin/manager only.
LlmUsageSummary.title: LlmUsageSummary

LlmUsageUseCaseStat.description: Token totals for one use-case bucket within the window.
LlmUsageUseCaseStat.title: LlmUsageUseCaseStat

MediaDownloadOut.description:
Short-lived presigned URL for an inbound message's mirrored media —
the SPA redirects the browser there to stream it straight from S3.
MediaDownloadOut.title: MediaDownloadOut

MembershipOut.description: User's membership in an org — what the switcher renders.
MembershipOut.title: MembershipOut

MergeFieldOut.description: One entry in the merge-field catalog, for the UI field picker.
MergeFieldOut.title: MergeFieldOut

MergeRequest.description:
Fold `loser_ids` into `survivor_id`: children re-parent to the
survivor, the losers are soft-deleted. Survivor's own fields are
left untouched (field-level merge is a UI concern, out of scope).
MergeRequest.title: MergeRequest

MessageStatus.description:
Lifecycle. Inbound messages are born `received`. Outbound messages
walk pending → sent → delivered → read (driven by Meta status webhooks),
or → failed.
MessageStatus.title: MessageStatus

MfaDisableRequest.description:
Disabling MFA requires the current password (prevents
drive-by-removal if access cookie is stolen) plus a current TOTP
or backup code (proves the user controls the second factor too).
MfaDisableRequest.title: MfaDisableRequest

MfaEnableOut.description:
Returned ONCE after /mfa/enable — backup codes in plaintext.
They are never returned again from any endpoint.
MfaEnableOut.title: MfaEnableOut

MfaEnableRequest.description:
User echoes the first 6-digit code from their authenticator app
to prove the secret made it across correctly.
MfaEnableRequest.title: MfaEnableRequest

MfaSetupOut.description:
Returned by POST /api/auth/mfa/setup. The `secret` is shown to
the user (manual-entry fallback if QR scanning fails); the
`provisioning_uri` is what the QR code encodes.
MfaSetupOut.title: MfaSetupOut

MfaVerifyRequest.description:
Second-step of login. `mfa_token` is the short-lived JWT issued
by /login when MFA is required; `code` is either a TOTP or a
backup code (decided by length).
MfaVerifyRequest.title: MfaVerifyRequest

NoteCreate.description:
POST /api/notes body. `organization_id` is NEVER read from
the client; resolved server-side from `get_current_org_id`.
NoteCreate.title: NoteCreate

NoteOut.description:
One note row. `author_name` / `author_email` denormalized off
the User JOIN so the UI doesn't N+1.
NoteOut.title: NoteOut

NotificationCounts.description:
Lightweight payload for the header poll. Cheaper than
fetching the full list when all the bell needs is the badge
count.
NotificationCounts.title: NotificationCounts

NotificationOut.description:
One in-app notification rendered in the header bell.
`actor_name` is denormalized from the User JOIN.
NotificationOut.title: NotificationOut

OrgOut.description: Public-ish view of an Organization (the user must be a member).
OrgOut.title: OrgOut

OutboxEventOut.description:
One outbox row, surfaced via the admin /api/outbox endpoint.
`payload` ships as the raw JSON string (already serialised by
the producer) — the UI parses + pretty-prints on display.
OutboxEventOut.title: OutboxEventOut

PasswordResetConfirm.description:
Body of POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm. The `token` is the
URL-safe credential delivered out-of-band; `new_password` replaces
the user's current hash unconditionally on success.
PasswordResetConfirm.title: PasswordResetConfirm

PipelineCreate.description:
POST /api/pipelines body. The new pipeline starts empty —
stages are added via the PATCH endpoint or by cloning the
default pipeline (clone helper is a follow-up).
PipelineCreate.title: PipelineCreate

PipelineStageOut.description: One column of a pipeline kanban.
PipelineStageOut.title: PipelineStageOut

PipelineStageWrite.description:
Replace-the-whole-stage-list body. The PATCH /pipelines/{id}
endpoint accepts a list of these and the backend reconciles
creates/updates/deletes against the existing rows by `id` —
missing ids are deletes, present ids are updates, null ids are
creates. Simpler from the UI's perspective than three separate
endpoints.
PipelineStageWrite.title: PipelineStageWrite

PipelineUpdate.description:
PATCH /api/pipelines/{id} body. Stages are an optional full
replacement — if `stages` is None, only the metadata fields
are updated.
PipelineUpdate.title: PipelineUpdate

QuoteStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a quote/proposal (ADR-016).

State machine (enforced in `app/api/quotes.py`):
    draft ──send──▶ sent ──accept──▶ accepted
                      │  └─decline──▶ declined
                      └────expire──▶ expired
`draft` is the only editable state. Once sent the document is
immutable — a "resend with changes" clones it into a new version
(the old row keeps its terminal state and points at the new one
via `superseded_by`).
QuoteStatus.title: QuoteStatus

QuoteUpdate.description:
Draft-only edits. The route rejects edits to a non-draft quote
(a sent/accepted revision is immutable — resend creates a new
version instead). All fields optional; `line_items`, when provided,
fully replaces the existing set.
QuoteUpdate.title: QuoteUpdate

RegisterResponse.description:
Body of POST /api/auth/register.

Two outcomes share this shape so the frontend can branch on a single
field:

  - `verification_required=True` (the common self-signup case): the
    user must confirm their email before logging in. No session is
    started, so `token` is null. The frontend shows a "check your
    email" screen.
  - `verification_required=False` (the very first user / install
    founder, auto-verified): a full session was started and `token`
    carries the access token, so the frontend logs them straight in.

`user` is always present so the frontend can read the resolved locale
for the post-signup redirect.
RegisterResponse.title: RegisterResponse

SearchResults.description:
Unified global-search payload for the Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette — top
matches per entity type in a single response (see GET /api/search).
SearchResults.title: SearchResults

SendInteractiveRequest.description:
Send an interactive message: reply buttons (`interactive_type="button"`,
1-3 buttons) or a list menu (`"list"`, up to 10 rows total across sections).

Both are session messages — only deliverable INSIDE the 24h window, same as
free-form text. The Meta size caps live on the nested models; this validator
enforces that the fields present match the chosen type and that the reply
ids are unique (a duplicate id makes the inbound reply ambiguous).
SendInteractiveRequest.title: SendInteractiveRequest

SendMediaRequest.description:
Send an outbound media message (image / document / video / audio).

Source the media EITHER by ``link`` (a public https URL Meta fetches) OR by
``media_id`` (a handle from an earlier upload to Meta) — exactly one. We do
NOT proxy bytes through our backend; the link route is the common case (e.g.
a hosted/presigned file URL). ``caption`` is honoured for image/video/
document only; ``filename`` for document only (both ignored otherwise so a
stray field is forgiving, not a 422).
SendMediaRequest.title: SendMediaRequest

SendMessageRequest.description:
Agent-composed outbound text. Capped at WhatsApp's ~4096-char body.

`reply_to_message_id` (one of our Message UUIDs in the same conversation)
sends this as a quoted reply threaded under that message.
SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest

SendReactionRequest.description:
React to a message with a single emoji. The target message is named by
the URL (`/messages/{message_id}/reaction`), so only the emoji is in the
body. An empty string removes a previously sent reaction (Meta's
convention); any non-empty value must be a single emoji grapheme — we don't
validate the unicode here, Meta rejects a non-emoji with a send error.
SendReactionRequest.title: SendReactionRequest

SendTemplateRequest.description:
Send a pre-approved WhatsApp message template — the ONLY way to message a
contact outside the 24h customer-service window (a free-form text there is
rejected by Meta).

``template_name`` + ``language_code`` identify an approved template in the
WABA. ``body_params`` fills the template's positional ``{{1}}``, ``{{2}}`` …
body placeholders in order; leave it empty for a template with no variables.
We don't fetch the template catalog, so an unknown name / wrong placeholder
count surfaces as a Meta send error on the message row.
SendTemplateRequest.title: SendTemplateRequest

SessionOut.description:
One active session for the authenticated user. `id` is the
opaque session_id (SHA-256-derived); the underlying refresh token
is never exposed. `current=True` for the session calling
/sessions — used by the SPA to disable the "revoke" button on
the user's own row.
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SignatureRequestCreate.description:
Raise a signing envelope against a quote OR a contract. Provide
exactly one of `quote_id` / `contract_id`; the document must be `sent`
(you sign a delivered proposal/agreement, not a draft). The provider is
taken from server config, never the client.
SignatureRequestCreate.title: SignatureRequestCreate

SignatureSignContext.description:
The minimal, unauthenticated view the signer sees on the signing
page — no internal ids, owners, or org plumbing. Works for both quote
and contract envelopes via the generic `document_*` fields. Marks the
request `viewed` as a side effect of being fetched.
SignatureSignContext.title: SignatureSignContext

SignatureSignIn.description:
Payload the manual in-app signer submits. The typed full name is the
consent record; IP / user-agent are captured server-side from the
request, never trusted from the body.
SignatureSignIn.title: SignatureSignIn

SignatureStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an e-signature request / envelope (ADR-016).

State machine (enforced in `app/api/signatures.py`):
    drafted ──send──▶ sent ──view──▶ viewed ──sign──▶ signed (terminal)
                        │               │
                        └────decline────┴──▶ declined (terminal)
    (drafted|sent|viewed) ──cancel──▶ cancelled (terminal)

`signed` is the completion state — all required parties have signed.
A separate `countersigned` is reserved for a future counter-signature
step (org signs after the customer) and is not yet reachable, mirroring
how `QuoteStatus.expired` is declared ahead of its transition.
SignatureStatus.title: SignatureStatus

TagBulk.description: Add/remove a set of tags across a set of entities of one type.
TagBulk.title: TagBulk

TeamCreate.description:
POST /api/teams body. Slug is auto-derived from name if
omitted; clients can supply one explicitly to control the URL
segment (future /teams/{slug} routing).
TeamCreate.title: TeamCreate

TeamMemberOut.description: One team member surfaced on TeamOut.members.
TeamMemberOut.title: TeamMemberOut

TeamOut.description:
A team plus its current member list. Counts are surfaced so
the UI can render "Inbound EU · 4 members" without a second
round-trip; the members array itself is included for the
expanded settings view.
TeamOut.title: TeamOut

WebhookDeliveryOut.description:
One delivery attempt — surfaces in the admin "recent deliveries"
table on the webhook detail page.
WebhookDeliveryOut.title: WebhookDeliveryOut

WebhookDeliveryStats.description:
Aggregate delivery health for one endpoint over a recent window,
surfaced on the webhook detail/settings card. Counts come from the
`webhook_deliveries` rows whose `scheduled_for` falls in the window;
`success_rate` is over terminal (success+failed) attempts only so a
burst of still-pending rows doesn't skew it.
WebhookDeliveryStats.title: WebhookDeliveryStats

WebhookEndpointCreate.description:
Admin creates an outgoing webhook for the current org.

`enabled_events` is a list of `EventType` slugs (e.g.
"lead.created") or `["*"]` for "every event". An empty list
is rejected (would be a silent no-op subscription).
WebhookEndpointCreate.title: WebhookEndpointCreate

WebhookEndpointCreated.description:
One-time response on POST /api/webhooks that includes the
plaintext `secret` so the admin can copy it into their receiver.
Future GETs return WebhookEndpointOut only.
WebhookEndpointCreated.title: WebhookEndpointCreated

WebhookEndpointOut.description:
Public view of a webhook endpoint. Secret is NOT included —
it's shown ONCE on create via WebhookEndpointCreated and never
again. Mirrors Stripe / GitHub UX.
WebhookEndpointOut.title: WebhookEndpointOut

WebhookEndpointUpdate.description:
PATCH endpoint — only mutable fields. `secret` rotation lives
on a dedicated POST .../rotate-secret route (not here) so it's
intentional, not buried in a generic patch.
WebhookEndpointUpdate.title: WebhookEndpointUpdate

WebhookTestResult.description:
Outcome of a synchronous `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/test` ping.

A test ping is delivered inline (not via the worker) so the admin
sees the receiver's HTTP status immediately. It records a
`WebhookDelivery` row (event_type `webhook.test`) for the history
table but intentionally does NOT touch `consecutive_failures` /
auto-pause — a failed test must not pause a real endpoint.
WebhookTestResult.title: WebhookTestResult

WhatsAppAccountConnect.description:
Connect a tenant's WhatsApp number. `access_token` is the permanent
(system-user) token — write-only: accepted here, never echoed back.
WhatsAppAccountConnect.title: WhatsAppAccountConnect

WhatsAppAccountOut.description: Account view for the settings UI. NEVER includes `access_token`.
WhatsAppAccountOut.title: WhatsAppAccountOut

WhatsAppBusinessProfileOut.description:
The public business profile customers see (the "about" card). All fields
are optional — a freshly-connected number may have none set yet.
``profile_picture_url`` is read-only (uploaded out-of-band).
WhatsAppBusinessProfileOut.title: WhatsAppBusinessProfileOut

WhatsAppBusinessProfileUpdate.description:
Patch editable business-profile fields. Omit a field to leave it
untouched — only fields explicitly set are sent on to Meta.
WhatsAppBusinessProfileUpdate.title: WhatsAppBusinessProfileUpdate

WhatsAppTemplateOut.description: One approved (or pending/rejected) message template, flattened for the UI.
WhatsAppTemplateOut.title: WhatsAppTemplateOut

get.description:
Return the activity timeline for a single entity, newest
first. Org-scoped — a foreign-org `entity_id` simply returns an
empty list (we don't 404 because the entity itself might not
exist; the caller already had to find the id from somewhere).

schema.title: Response List Activities Api Activities Get

get.description: Return dead jobs, most recent first.

schema.title: Response List Dlq Api Admin Dlq Get
Response Dlq Count Api Admin Dlq Count Get
Response List Api Keys Api Api Keys Get

delete.description:
Soft-revoke: stamp `revoked_at`. Idempotent — revoking an already
revoked key is a no-op that returns the current state. Returns the
key (not 204) so the UI can reflect the revoked timestamp without a
re-fetch.

post.description:
SSE streaming endpoint — yields `data: {"token": "..."}` lines.
Ends with `data: [DONE]`. Errors are sent as `data: {"error": "..."}` then DONE.

schema.title: Response List Attachments Api Attachments Get

get.description:
Return a short-lived presigned URL. The SPA redirects the
browser there, and the file streams directly from S3 — no
bytes flow through this API process.

schema.title: Response List Audit Api Audit Get

post.description:
Join an org using an invite token without creating a new account.

The logged-in user's email must match the invite email. On success
the user gains membership in the inviting org and their
`last_active_org_id` is updated to it.
post.summary: Accept an org invite while already logged in

post.description:
Verifies password. If the user has MFA enabled, returns a
short-lived `mfa_token` instead of a full session — the client
follows up with /mfa/verify. Otherwise returns the full session
(cookies + body) as before.

Response shape depends on MFA state, so the return type is
intentionally untyped at the FastAPI layer (frontend type-narrows
on the `mfa_required` field).

Records the logout event, revokes the refresh token in Redis,
and clears all session cookies.

The current access JWT continues to validate via signature alone
until it expires (15 min default) — a leaked access token survives
that long. Revoking it server-side instantly would require either
a per-request Redis hit (every protected endpoint) or a JTI-based
blocklist with the same cost. We accept the 15-minute window.

Remove MFA. Requires the current password (proves the cookie
isn't drive-by-stolen) plus a current TOTP or backup code (proves
the second factor is genuinely accessible to the requester).
Both checks are required — either alone would let an attacker who
has only one factor remove the other.

Activate MFA after the user proves the secret made it across
by submitting the first code from their authenticator. Generates
10 single-use backup codes and returns them in plaintext ONCE —
they are never returned by any subsequent endpoint.

Generate (and store) a fresh secret for this user. The secret
is NOT considered active until /mfa/enable validates the first
code — until then, login still works without MFA. Re-running
setup overwrites the pending secret (useful if the user lost the
QR mid-flow).

Second step of MFA login. Validates the challenge token + a
TOTP code OR a backup code, and on success starts a full session.

schema.title: Response Providers Api Auth Oauth Providers Get

post.description:
Consume a reset token to set a new password.

Failure modes use distinct codes so the UI can render specific
messages without leaking which step failed for an attacker (the
rate limit + opaque error text upstream provides the leak
defense; 404 vs 410 here is a UX nicety for legitimate users):
  - unknown / never-existed token → 404
  - already used token → 410 Gone
  - expired token → 410 Gone

Defense-in-depth: a per-token Redis counter invalidates the token
after 10 failed attempts, preventing brute-force across multiple
IPs that would otherwise bypass the per-IP SlowAPI limit.

Send (log, today) a password-reset link to the given email.

Always returns 204 — even if the email is unknown — to avoid
leaking which addresses have accounts. The token is delivered
out-of-band; in dev the URL is emitted on the log line
`password_reset.dispatched` for the operator to copy/paste.

Mint a fresh access token from the refresh cookie AND rotate
the refresh token itself. Detects reuse of already-rotated
tokens as a theft signal and revokes the entire user's sessions.

Steps:
  1. Read the path-scoped `refresh_token` cookie.
  2. Look up the token in Redis:
     * VALID → mint new access JWT, rotate the refresh token
       (atomic: new token issued, old token deleted and
       tombstoned for 5 min), reset both cookies.
     * MISSING + matches a recent tombstone → REUSE DETECTED.
       Revoke EVERY session for this user (someone is replaying
       a refresh token; the legitimate client moved on, and we
       don't know which side is the attacker). Audit + 401.
     * MISSING + no tombstone → ordinary expired/revoked path.
       Plain 401.

Two-tab race: the legitimate second tab may innocently replay
the just-rotated token. With a 5-min tombstone we'd revoke its
sessions — false positive. Mitigation lives at the SPA layer:
`lib/api.ts` collapses concurrent 401s into a SINGLE in-flight
/refresh call (already implemented). The server-side replay
detection is the last line of defence — false positives here
are acceptable since the user can re-login.

CSRF: the global middleware enforces X-CSRF-Token here too,
because this is a state-changing POST (it mints a new
credential).

Create a new user account AND attach it to the inviting org in
one atomic transaction. Same rate limit as /login to deter brute-
forcing tokens via this endpoint.

Scope for now: this endpoint is for NEW email addresses only. Adding
an existing logged-in user to a new org via invite is a separate
Phase 4b feature (would need an authenticated "accept" endpoint).

get.description:

delete.description:
Revoke a specific session (= log out one specific device).

doesn't exist OR belongs to another user (no enumeration).

post.description:
Consume a verification token to mark the user's email confirmed,

Token validation mirrors confirm_password_reset's distinct codes so
the UI can render a precise dead-link message:

  - already used token → 410 Gone
  - expired token → 410 Gone

On success we start a full session (cookies + body) so clicking the
link in the email lands the user in the dashboard without a second
login step.

Re-send the verification link for an unconfirmed account.

Always returns 204 — even if the email is unknown, the account is
disabled, or it's already verified — to avoid leaking which addresses
have accounts or their verification state. A fresh token is minted +
emailed only when the email maps to an active, not-yet-verified user.

terminated / expired) — you don't re-issue something still being
drafted; just edit it. The new revision copies the terms, keeps the
same `number`, and starts as `draft`; the prior row points forward

Terminate a signed or active contract.

The one transition with two valid source states — you can kill an
agreement that was signed but never activated, or one already in
force. `_transition` only checks a single `from_status`, so this is
handled inline.

Dedicated route (not folded into PATCH) so rotation is always an

Returns the new plaintext secret ONCE, exactly like create; the old
secret stops signing immediately, so the receiver must be updated in

Send a synthetic `webhook.test` event to the endpoint, inline.

table but does NOT mutate `consecutive_failures` / `last_*_at` — a
test must not nudge a healthy endpoint toward auto-pause. Works even
while the endpoint is paused (that's the point: verify before
unpausing).

post.description:
Inbound messages + delivery-status callbacks from Meta.

Always returns 200 once the signature checks out — even when nothing
matched a known number — so Meta stops retrying. A bad/absent signature is
403; an unconfigured app secret is 503. We never trust the parsed JSON for
auth: the HMAC is computed over the EXACT received bytes.

get.description: Liveness probe — process is up.

Readiness probe — fails fast if any required dep is unhealthy.

Components:
  * `db`     — required. Postgres is fatal; without it nothing works.
  * `redis`  — required. Sessions and refresh-tokens live there;
               without it auth itself starts failing within minutes.
  * `llm`    — optional. We probe Ollama (or the configured LLM
               provider) for completeness, but a missing LLM
               degrades AI features rather than killing the
               service. Marked `degraded`, not `down`, on miss.

Returns 503 when any REQUIRED component is down. The body always
surfaces a per-component map so monitoring can attribute outages
without re-probing each dep.
